messages:
maria: heads-up — I'm trying to roll a scheduled capacity bump for the nv4b GPU pool (12 -> 24) to support a benchmark next week. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4388
sam: saw the PR, pipeline failed the premerge gate. can you paste the conftest output?
maria: pasted the failing snippet:
```
FAIL - resources.tf:12 - deny[\"freeze_window\"] - modification of gpu pool not allowed during infra freeze
Rule: deny[msg] {
  input.change.type == \"terraform\"
  input.resource.tags[_] == \"gpu-pool\"
  now >= freeze_window.start
  now <= freeze_window.end
}
```
cheng: that's the freeze-window policy kicking in. The monthly freeze spans 1806000000 - 1806500000. We block pool size changes to avoid churn during infra ops.
natalie: is this an emergency or planned? If planned, we should either reschedule or request an exemption.
maria: it's planned — benchmark run is vendor-scheduled and only fits next Tuesday. We need the extra capacity staged across off-peak hours.
sam: two options:
• reschedule the benchmark outside the freeze window
• file an ops policy exemption (requires infra-approver + SRE lead acknowledgement)
ops-bot: :robot_face: Policy violation: freeze-window. To request a scoped exception, open an INFOPOL ticket and include PR link + mitigation plan.
maria: opened INFOPOL-792 with rollout plan and cost estimate: https://issues.internal/INFOPOL-792
cheng: proposal: allow scoped, auditable exemptions using PR metadata label `policy:exempt:<TICKET>`. Premerge hook will accept the change only if the ticket shows APPROVED by infra and SRE leads.
sam: I like scoped labels. we should require both approver usernames and ticket closure state. No silent bypass.
natalie: what's the blast radius? doubling nv4b could increase preemptible consumption and cause regional scheduling pressure in us-west2. finance OK'd benchmark cost but we should do a phased scale: 12 -> 16 -> 20 -> 24 across 3 windows.
maria: updating terraform to use phased counts and adding a canary target group `gpu-benchmark-canary`. will push a commit.
conftest-bot: premerge check re-run: FAIL (freeze-window) — missing `policy:exempt:INFOPOL-792` label.
maria: added label `policy:exempt:INFOPOL-792` and added a short note in the ticket with approver names. pinging @sre-lead and @infra-approver for approval.
sre-lead: approved INFOPOL-792. please proceed but gate to canary and monitor node/pod evictions for 30m after each step.
oncall: oncall +1. will watch incidents channel during the rollout.
ops-bot: :robot_face: Verified INFOPOL-792 status: APPROVED by sre-lead, infra-approver. Allow flag set for PR 4388 until 1806007200.
conftest-bot: premerge checks re-run: PASS (freeze-window exemption INFOPOL-792 verified).
maria: rolling out in 3 stages now. dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/gpu/nv4b — will post updates.
natalie: please capture any scheduling failures and incremental cost in the ticket; we'll follow-up with a short post-run note for finance.
cheng: opened a follow-up PR to extend the premerge hook to parse `policy:exempt` labels and validate ticket status via the issues API. it still requires approver signatures. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/4391
sam: thanks — that should reduce manual steps next time. lesson: schedule capacity ops outside freeze windows when possible, otherwise follow exemption flow early. :thumbsup:
maria: marking thread resolved — INFOPOL-792 closed, canary reached target sizes, no evictions observed, final pool at 24 after phased rollout. will add a short post-run note in the ticket.
